The vibrant growth of Hong Kong's sustainable bond activities is partly attributable to the demonstrative effect of the Government Green Bond Programme. Since 2019, the HKMA has helped the Government issue green bonds worth approximately US$25 billion, sold to institutional and retail investors. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds—including currency denominations, tenors and distribution channels—laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bonds in 2022, we issued the world's first batch of tokenised government green bond in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the issuance of the second batch of tokenised green bond; this batch was denominated in four major currencies and issued in a digitally native form, making it the world's first multi-currency digital green bond. At the same time, we have proactively introduced various measures to enhance the vibrancy and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. This spans work in a number of areas including skills training, data enhancement, green fintech and transition finance. In particular, in the area of talent development, in 2023 we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking practitioners, providing systematic courses to enhance their understanding of and expertise in green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key area of our work; it provides funding for decarbonisation activities in high-carbon-emitting and hard-to-abate industries, preventing these industries from being unable to transition due to a lack of financial support. To support the sound development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong's green classification framework to cover transition activities. We will also expand the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme, which provides subsidies to eligible bond issuers and borrowers, to include transition bonds and loans, so as to encourage enterprises in the region to raise transition funds in Hong Kong. In addition, we will strengthen communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders, and through public-private collaboration and blended finance models, attract private-sector investment in sustainable development projects that have traditionally found it difficult to secure financing. Some of the above work requires cross-sectoral collaboration, and is primarily coordinated by the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, which is co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-standing collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the Alliance for Green Commercial Banks, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office also joined the Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance and the Green Investment and Financing Partnership as a founding member in 2023. In addition, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero also announced plans to set up a chapter in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we hope to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, and in turn support the channelling of funds to sustainable development projects in the region and around the world. To promote new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also helped host the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week earlier this year, attracting more than 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including top decision-makers in the global business and financial arenas, to jointly discuss solutions for scaling up climate financing in the region and to forge new partnerships in this regard. Chief Executive Mr Eddie Yue delivered a speech at the Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum, a flagship event of the Hong Kong Green Week. As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a globally significant asset owner, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of green and sustainable asset investment, and has progressively expanded the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset portfolios in the public and private markets. In pursuit of the goal for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA added last year an actively managed global equity portfolio themed on sustainability and climate transition, while extending the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another public-market asset portfolio. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds that the HKMA has prioritised for investment have outperformed their investment benchmarks, embodying the notion of "doing well by doing good". In the private markets, we have continued to pursue green-related investment opportunities and became an anchor investor in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. At the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio was 6% and 46% lower than the 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently remained below the overall market level. As a sustainable organisation, the HKMA will continue to strive for improvement, setting our sustainable development goals and plans on the basis of the three pillars of environment, staff and social responsibility. Specifically, on its low-carbon transition journey, the HKMA continuously strengthens its capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emissions reduction, improving energy efficiency and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have already formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the short term, and have made good progress towards our medium-term target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain outstanding talent to fulfil the HKMA's various important functions, in addition to its green goals, the HKMA is also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of its staff. Furthermore, by working with various stakeholders, we contribute to building a caring society by promoting financial inclusion, enhancing citizens' financial literacy, and raising public awareness of guarding against financial fraud. The climate challenge is enormous and exceptionally urgent. Economies around the world are moving towards a more sustainable future, a process that is expected to bring about tremendous changes in financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries no small risk, but will also be accompanied by unprecedented opportunities. As a major global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to lead the way in taking action to address these challenges. At the same time, we are also well positioned to ride on this momentum. The HKMA will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition; and will continue to lead by example as a responsible investor and a sustainable organisation, and to work with like-minded partners to advance this global agenda that is of the utmost importance at present. Chief Executive Eddie Yue

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are of global concern. The HKMA's goal in its sustainability work is to strive to play a leadership role through its own policies and operations, ensuring that Hong Kong's financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to the risks of climate change, and supporting the transition to more sustainable economic development. Through active participation in international and regional organisations, the HKMA will also strive to contribute to the formulation of regional and even global green and sustainable finance policies and standards. As the regulator of the banking sector, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking sector's climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. Specifically, the priority work items include: launching a new round of thematic review on banks' climate risk management practices, and conducting a new round of consultation sessions as part of reviewing banks' progress in implementing climate risk management supervisory requirements; continuing the work on incorporating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; completing the second round of the industry-wide climate risk stress-tested exercise, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including working with relevant local authorities to align the relevant requirements with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards, which serve as the global baseline, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Pillar 3 framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on best practices for transition planning with the industry. To promote the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the HKMA will continue to keep abreast of local and international market and regulatory developments, and maintain communication with the industry to ensure that banks adopt appropriate sales processes. In addition, the HKMA will also play a facilitator role, striving to promote the development of the green finance ecosystem and support banks in providing financing for economic transition. We will soon publish the local green taxonomy and continue to expand its coverage to include more activities such as transition activities. At the same time, we will also continue to explore the application of technology solutions to help banks identify, measure and monitor their climate risk exposures; one example is the upcoming cloud-based platform, which will facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance the professional capabilities of practitioners, in 2024 we will also develop the professional level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners". Hong Kong is well positioned to serve as a regional and international sustainable finance hub. To fulfil this role, the HKMA is assisting the Government in implementing the recommendations in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope covered by the "Government Green Bond Programme" to sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bonds market; at the same time, it will attract more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme". We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions and enterprises to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and explore the potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to assist in implementing the Government-funded "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme" to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. As co-chairs of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group" (Steering Group), we will continue to work closely with other agencies and departments to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and work on promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Group will focus its work on three areas, including sustainability disclosure, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another work priority, through the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks", the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will continue to jointly launch various dedicated programmes in the Asian region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and providing practical guidance to help banks support financial institutions in establishing their tailored green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our cooperation with the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero", the "Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance", and the "Green Investment and Financing Partnership". As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's portfolio by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of the Exchange Fund's investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring that the resilience of the asset portfolio is maintained on the path towards net zero. We fully understand that achieving the goals of the "Paris Agreement" requires an overall economic transition, and therefore we are optimising our net-zero strategy, focusing on assets that can bring positive climate benefits to the real economy, while taking into account the Exchange Fund's investment objectives. As an environmentally responsible institution, the HKMA's decarbonisation strategy will continue to evolve with the times, to reflect the latest market, regulatory, technological and other climate-related developments. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage staff to participate in our sustainability work, including launching campaigns to develop sustainable habits and optimising office processes and practices. Furthermore, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices when selecting and renewing contracts. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA is committed to upholding the specified certification standards. As for the regular upgrading of data centre facilities, in addition to keeping abreast of the latest technological developments, we will also incorporate green design and practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and technology convergence, and actively modernise internal systems to improve efficiency and minimise potential risks as far as possible. Finally, in terms of the social focus area, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for colleagues, and work with the industry to promote financial inclusion and improve financial literacy, as well as raise public awareness of guarding against financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to reducing its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, a banking sector regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor and a sustainable organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the entire Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework that leads the formulation of the HKMA's related strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of relevant measures, and ensures that sustainability considerations are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In its commitment to practising sound corporate governance, the HKMA has put in place a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms for monitoring and assessing the progress and effectiveness of its sustainability work. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for monitoring the HKMA's work—including its work on sustainability—and making recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; on responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and, in respect of other functional areas, relevant teams and working groups, which are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures relating to banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), jointly initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability initiatives over the past few years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a brand-new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all of the HKMA's sustainability work across its different functional areas.1 It provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking sector, market development, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's functional departments; assesses the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and oversees the external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives as permanent members. In addition, we invite the Assistant Chief Executives responsible for the key functions relating to green and sustainability matters to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on the major achievements of their work and their future plans. The Steering Committee holds regular meetings and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's banking departments, the Corporate Development and Operations Department, the External Department and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC jointly initiated the Steering Group in May 2020.2 As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts on the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, so as to consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change is a significant risk facing the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations. To continue to fulfil their important functions in the financial system and channel more funds towards green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risk. As the regulator of the banking sector, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capabilities to respond to and manage climate risk, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. The HKMA is committed to formulating various policy measures to strengthen the banking system's capabilities to respond to climate risk. In August, the HKMA issued a circular on net-zero transition planning, setting out high-level principles to help banks maintain safety and soundness during the process of transitioning the economy to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of the circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey of selected banks in the fourth quarter to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices on transition planning with the industry, and will organise seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experiences within the industry. In terms of disclosure requirements, in response to the latest international developments, including the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards announced in June, as well as the consultation launched in November by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (the Basel Committee) on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks, the HKMA is enhancing its related work to improve the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is working with relevant local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that aligns with the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards. During the year, the HKMA strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to banks to help them further enhance their capabilities in climate resilience and climate risk management. The HKMA made significant progress in implementing the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into banking supervisory processes. Climate risk management has now become a standing agenda item at prudential supervisory meetings held with banks' management. Banking supervisors also adopt an enhanced CAMEL rating system1 that has incorporated climate risk factors to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of implementing the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into banking supervisory processes, the HKMA revised its "green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, in order to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to respond to climate risk. Among the key work priorities under the 2023 two-year plan, following the conclusion of the 12-month implementation period for compliance with module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual, the HKMA launched a round of thematic examinations on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. This thematic examination covered four major areas, including the governance structure for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and institutional culture, awareness and communication. The HKMA made several improvements to its climate risk stress-tested framework, including introducing a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of the simultaneous occurrence of economic and climate change shocks. Following these improvements and as part of the HKMA's regular supervisor-driven stress-tested programme, the second round of climate risk stress-tested was launched in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and further enhance banks' capabilities to manage climate risk. A total of 44 banks participated in this round of risk stress-tested, an increase of more than 60% compared with the first pilot programme in 2021. The HKMA also organised a Climate Risk Stress-tested Forum in November, which was attended by as many as 300 banking practitioners. By facilitating the sharing of experiences among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk quantification. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing the HKMA's module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The HKMA held meetings with banks' management to discuss their work on climate risk management and the common challenges facing the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other publicly available information to assess their related progress. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue to strengthen their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's supervisory expectations. As the world increasingly focuses on climate change and strives to address related issues, the HKMA has observed a growing demand for green and sustainable investment products, and some banks have also offered related products to meet customer demand. In view of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' sales of green and sustainable investment products, and issued a circular in November setting out the standards the HKMA expects banks to achieve and sharing the good practices observed. This circular covers a range of areas including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training and record-keeping, and aims to reduce potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of related investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can enhance data availability and risk analysis, strengthening banks' capabilities to manage climate risk. The HKMA will soon launch a pilot version of a cloud-based platform to enable banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. In addition, the HKMA continues to work with other central banks and regulators to explore how technological solutions can assist in physical risk assessments. On the other hand, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) approaches through the application of advanced analytics and A.I. to reduce the use of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby strengthening banks' operational processes for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA organised the "Green Fintech Competition", aimed at seeking market-ready solutions to help the banking sector address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted a total of more than 85 entries from about 70 companies. In December, the HKMA organised the "Green and Sustainable Banking Conference" to provide a platform for the banking sector and the technology sector to explore the role of low-carbon technologies and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and the Mainland, and announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition" at the same event. This event attracted about 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and to make green and sustainable finance decisions more consistent, the HKMA developed a local green taxonomy framework with the assistance of a consultancy firm. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype of the Hong Kong Green Classification Framework" to seek stakeholders' views on establishing and implementing a green taxonomy catalogue. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the prototype framework and identifying other areas for the next stage of the framework's development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force, which has recognised environmental crimes as predicate offences for money laundering, and in view of the interconnectedness between AML and environmental, social and governance (ESG), this area is receiving increasing attention from more regulators. The HKMA is well aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and therefore has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing monitoring work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, and incorporates analysis of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the scenario design and analysis workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA helps to further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the macroeconomic and financial impacts of climate change. As a member of the transition planning working group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participates in analysing the interplay between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to develop a forward-looking and dynamic perspective in examining climate-related financial risks. In terms of research work, the HKMA has conducted a number of applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. Research topics include the climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG fund flows3, the impact of climate change on housing prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in the global supply chain5. The above research findings enhance the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, and help inform the formulation of related policies. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risk on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares its research findings with a wide range of stakeholders through various channels such as international activities on climate-related matters and the HKMA Research Memorandum. The HKMA's Liquidity Facilities Framework is a collateralised standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. In line with the NGFS's recommendations, the HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations when assessing eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on responding to climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through this engagement, the HKMA helps to promote international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws on the insights gained to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. During the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to jointly build a richer ecosystem and promote the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategy. The Steering Group has made good progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing sustainable finance opportunities, with major areas of work including sustainability disclosure, strengthening the ecosystem, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainability Disclosure Working Group has been established to formulate a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will cover four key areas, including sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. A Transition Finance Working Group has also been established to explore ways to support financial institutions and enterprises in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Group also strengthens the building of the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sector skills training and data enhancement. In particular, on the data front, we continue to promote the adoption of the climate and environmental risk questionnaire for non-listed corporates launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to keep abreast of the latest developments in the field of green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub in the region and globally. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to seize the investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia Pacific region. To facilitate skills training in the industry, the Centre for Green and Sustainable Finance under the Steering Group implemented the Government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Programme", providing subsidies for practitioners, students, and graduates who undertake green and sustainable finance-related training and obtain relevant qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training courses or qualifications were registered as eligible training or qualifications under the programme, and over 560 subsidy applications were approved. The HKMA also launched a new Foundation-level module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the "Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners". This module aims to promote talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to work with the banking sector to develop the Professional-level of this module to meet the rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals in the industry. To help financial institutions and enterprises, especially small and medium-sized enterprises, better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning, during the year the HKMA collaborated with relevant Government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), to organise a series of seminars and thematic workshops, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. On the student front, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Programme" in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to deepen interns' and university undergraduate graduates' understanding of sustainable finance. The HKMA is well aware of the potential of technology in filling climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, and is therefore committed to making relevant data more accessible and improving data quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Group launched a series of website enhancement measures to provide financial institutions, enterprises, and the public with one-stop green and sustainable finance information. Key enhancements include a sustainability disclosure e-platform, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more focused, easy-to-browse and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week", the Steering Group also co-organised the "Harnessing Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance" event with Cyberport and Invest Hong Kong, showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week — Finance Theme" was held from 26 February to 1 March 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 jurisdictions, including representatives from financial institutions, enterprises, central banks, international organisations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms. The flagship event of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia Pacific Climate Business Forum" co-organised by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together over 400 guests, including top decision-makers from the global business and financial sectors, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia Pacific region. This two-day event explored a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonisation of heavy industries, the circular economy, the future development of sustainable finance, and new climate technologies in the emerging and developing markets of the Asia Pacific region. The forum received support from both public and private sector organisations, which co-organised more than 10 roundtables, seminars, and other exchange activities. Topics covered climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomy, and green development financing in Belt and Road regions. In addition, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund co-organised the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" on 29 February 2024 to explore key measures to scale up climate finance and the role of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. The above events form part of the HKMA's overall efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as a useful platform to help participants drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address the climate finance challenges in the Asia Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation and the HKMA launched the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks", a collaborative platform bringing together financial institutions, banking industry organisations, research institutions, and innovative technology providers in the region to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held 22 training events and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from around the world, including the Asia Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, together with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second frontier issues research report titled "Developing an Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategy: A Case Study". During the year, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office joined the newly established "Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment" (CASI) and the "Green Investment and Finance Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road Initiative Green Development International Coalition. Cooperation with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity training and knowledge sharing, and channel more funding towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and the broader region. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of a Hong Kong chapter to help support the net-zero efforts of financial institutions in Hong Kong and the Mainland. The HKMA assists GFANZ's work in an advisory role. To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. The HKMA assists in the issuance of green bonds under the programme. To date, the Government has issued green institutional and retail bonds equivalent to about US$25 billion, with the proceeds raised allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the programme, the Government publishes the "Green Bond Report" annually, detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from the green bonds and the expected environmental benefits. In the 2023-24 financial year, the Government continued its regular green institutional bond issuance work, issuing green bonds equivalent to about US$6 billion in June. This tri-currency issuance covered US dollar, euro, and renminbi bonds of various tenors, attracting different types of investors with an enthusiastic subscription response, recording a subscription amount equivalent to nearly US$30 billion. Among these, the issuance size of the renminbi bonds increased from RMB10 billion issued in January to RMB15 billion, and a 10-year renminbi bond was introduced for the first time, helping to extend the Government's renminbi yield curve and further enrich the range of offshore CNH products. The enthusiastic response of global investors to the Government's green bond issuance reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued the second batch of green Retail Bonds with a total value of HKD20 billion, further promoting market development and advancing inclusive finance. This issuance provided members of the public with an investment opportunity offering stable returns, enabling them to both participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the HKMA plays a pivotal role in advancing green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the HKMA has been at the forefront of green and sustainable asset investment, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership and to integrate environmental, social and governance factors into the investment management of the exchange Fund. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "Capital Preservation First, Long-Term Value Enhancement,"1 believing that giving full attention to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps to reduce related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to become a signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and to set a "Net Zero 2050" target2 for its "portfolio," the HKMA is committed to continually advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasising sustainability—particularly the pressing issue of climate change—with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the exchange Fund and pursuing more favourable risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA participates in building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem, partnering with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practice standards, and promoting the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and among central banks. Through stewardship and collaborative measures, the HKMA is committed to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. Exhibit 1: The exchange Fund's Responsible Investment Journey. Comprehensive and reliable ESG information is essential to integrating sustainability and to charting a credible climate transition to achieve net zero targets. To fulfil its commitments to the Network of Central Banks and Supervisors for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration3 and the strategic plan of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group, the HKMA leads by example, preparing this chapter on the responsible investment of the exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, sets the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the exchange Fund. The overarching guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks involved in the exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach and monitors the relevant implementation through regular meeting reports of the Sustainable Investment Team of the exchange Fund Investment Office. As illustrated in Exhibit 2, the ESG Committee under the exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategist, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring the various ESG initiatives of the exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and work progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Strategist of the exchange Fund Investment Office, convenes semi-annually to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures of the HKMA's various functions, including the exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to realise the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. Exhibit 2: The Responsible Investment Governance Structure of the exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Exhibit 1, the exchange Fund Investment Office embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could affect the financial performance of the exchange Fund. As sustainability rapidly evolved and moved beyond risk considerations to become a priority strategic focus for major institutions worldwide, the exchange Fund Investment Office revisited its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone, with the exchange Fund Investment Office establishing a new Business Strategy Division led by the Chief Strategist, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the exchange Fund Investment Office, and incorporating the responsible investment dedicated team formerly under the Risk Management and Compliance Department—now known as the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA's elevation of the focus of responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related matters in investment. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams of the exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors, and assists the senior staff of the exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG—particularly climate-related—risks and opportunities across various investments: Public Market Investments—the Credit, Compliance and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior staff of the exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models with reference to the views of the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG status of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team also participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment and monitoring process of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the section "Promoting the Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" under the "Risk Management" section on page 40). Private Market Investments—the Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams on each investment proposal. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks4 arising from climate change, as well as the related opportunities, will affect the long-term performance and value of the exchange Fund's investments. The 2023 Emissions Gap Report5 published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless there are further reductions in greenhouse gas emissions worldwide, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels before 2030. The pressing need for more aggressive policies, technological development or behavioural change to keep temperature rises in check may intensify transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranded asset shocks. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming more frequent and severe, posing additional physical risks to investments. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. In 2022, the HKMA set the target for the exchange Fund's "portfolio" to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged efforts, with a clear focus on decarbonisation and transition. These approaches are detailed in the following sections. Exhibit 3: The HKMA's Three-Pronged Approach to Responsible Investment. In progressing towards its net zero target, the HKMA is inclined to engage proactively rather than to exclude or divest from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the primary investment objective of the exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess outstanding technology and good corporate governance to cope with evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investments or divesting does not help resolve the carbon emissions problem. On the contrary, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, driving them to implement a transition to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing about beneficial changes for themselves and the world at large. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net zero investment strategies, adopting a comprehensive approach to pursue transition outcomes that align with the exchange Fund's and global net zero targets, while adhering to its guiding principles of responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to promote climate transition and to enhance the long-term resilience of the exchange Fund's asset portfolio (Exhibit 4). The HKMA's responsible investment maintained good momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a brand-new actively managed global equity portfolio themed on sustainability and climate transition, managed by external investment managers, and expanded the application of a customised low-carbon equity index to another portfolio managed by external investment managers. In addition, the green, social and sustainability bonds prioritised by the HKMA for investment outperformed the investment benchmark, demonstrating the concept of "doing well by doing good." In private markets, the HKMA actively builds a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities that are expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as climate and energy transition. For example, during the year the HKMA invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, reflecting the HKMA's commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs. Exhibit 4: Ongoing Implementation of Measures to Promote ESG Investment. The HKMA has invested in a company that specialises in producing eco-friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic matter such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike conventional chemical recycling systems that rely on energy-intensive high-temperature environments to produce plastics, this company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. This 100% waste-derived plastic material can serve as an alternative to the oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and durable consumer goods, offering a sustainable and versatile option. At the same time, this plastic material is also compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is a firm supporter of the circular economy. The HKMA committed two tranches of US dollar 1 billion each to the MCPP in 2017 and 2019 respectively, and further collaborated with the International Finance Corporation in 2021 to create a brand-new global climate-related investment platform, "MCPP One Planet," which is also the world's first cross-sector emerging-market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP programme, the HKMA has committed to providing loans to 80 sustainable development projects in 38 developing countries across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate and manufacturing. The International Finance Corporation has collected data on the MCPP loans. According to the International Finance Corporation's report, the HKMA's loan commitments provide support to emerging markets and developing countries in various areas such as economic transition and human resources development. Specifically, the projects to which the HKMA provides loans are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by about 5.6 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent per year, equivalent to the greenhouse gases emitted by an average petrol car driving 14 billion miles. The green and sustainable finance ecosystem is the cornerstone of future global sustainable development. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organisation and is adopting a multi-pronged approach to reducing its carbon footprint, with a target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also places importance on the physical and mental well-being of its staff and on social responsibility, and works to promote financial inclusion as well as to enhance the financial literacy of the public. As a responsible organisation, the HKMA has set sustainability goals under the three pillars of environment, staff and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), established in October, is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and is the principal decision-making body for the organisation's various sustainability initiatives. The predecessor of the Steering Committee was the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategies and policies for corporate sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Team provide support in coordinating the organisation's sustainability work; the former serves as a platform for discussing how to create a green working environment and for pooling ideas, while the latter aims to foster a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transformation path. The focus of the work is on implementing decarbonisation strategies in its day-to-day operations, including operating green buildings and data centres, practising green travel, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools and more environmentally friendly modes of operation, reducing waste, and building a culture of sustainability. The HKMA also plans to apply internal carbon pricing tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and to adopt carbon offset measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the above environmental commitments relating to its day-to-day operations, the HKMA continues to roll out more environmentally friendly operational solutions for the wider community, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and to make contact, as well as electronic payment and coin collection programmes for the general public. To strengthen and maintain its operational capacity, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and places importance on the physical and mental well-being of its staff. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages staff to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers the use of social enterprises (SEs) in procurement; promotes consumer education on financial services; and works with the banking sector to ensure that all sectors of society can gain fair access to basic banking services. The remainder of this chapter sets out details of each of the above strategies. Under the HKMA's overall enterprise risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats that the HKMA has to face in its day-to-day operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts brought about by climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by more extreme weather, may affect the HKMA's offices and hinder staff travel. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its business continuity plans to cope with extreme weather conditions. The HKMA also regularly conducts evacuation and back-up facility activation drills to ensure that staff are ready at all times to carry out business continuity measures. A number of measures have also been incorporated into the design of the offices to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy use, air travel and waste disposal. The HKMA has been monitoring the transition risks it is exposed to by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate target is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 (air travel) in all areas of the organisation's operations by 2050 or earlier. As near-term emission reduction targets, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all of its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and, using 2015 as the base year, to reduce its Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various decarbonisation and offset strategies. Despite the challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will nonetheless adopt a multi-pronged approach as far as practicable to minimise Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions (such as paper consumption, waste generation and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were developed with reference to the "Science Based Targets initiative" methodology, which has also been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The HKMA has appointed the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency to verify the emissions, energy and paper consumption, and waste data disclosed in this report. The scope of verification and the baselines are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the Annual Report 2022, the HKMA also independently published the Sustainability Report 2022 for the first time. The HKMA's efforts to enhance ESG reporting were recognised with an ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulator to win an award in this category. The judging panel commended the HKMA for meeting good ESG standards, for producing a Sustainability Report that is clear and easy to read, and for appointing an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report, reflecting its commitment to highly transparent and accountable reporting. In addition, the HKMA also received the highest rating, the Gold Award in the "Non-profit-making and Charitable Organisations" category, in the Hong Kong Management Association's "Best Annual Reports Awards 2023". The judging panel praised the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and for making good use of infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's determination to enhance financial literacy and promote financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's commitment to caring for the environment, its staff and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impacts arising from its operations, and its internal "Green Office Guidelines" provide staff with guidance on the use of resources and the generation of office waste. The HKMA has incorporated environmental considerations into the design, operation and maintenance of the offices it owns and leases. When renovating offices, existing furniture and fitting-out materials are reused as far as possible to reduce waste, and priority is given to the use of environmentally friendly building and decoration materials. The HKMA has consistently adopted this practice, and as a result, in 2021 and 2022 it was awarded Gold certification by LEED and BEAM Plus Interiors respectively for parts of its offices at Two International Finance Centre that had completed renovation. Improving energy efficiency through the adoption of new technologies and the good use of existing technologies remains one of the HKMA's key areas of focus. In addition to promoting good habits, such as switching off unnecessary lighting fixtures in work areas outside office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include the use of light-emitting diode (LED) lighting equipment, motion sensors, setting air-conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and making good use of energy in the IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has been decreasing continuously, standing at 2.59 MWh per capita in 2023, down 29.7% from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's day-to-day operations, its greenhouse gas emissions mainly arise from the consumption of electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuel and electricity was 1.48 tCO2e per capita, down 45.2% from 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardising equipment, office software and meeting facilities, the HKMA has also adopted digital tools and technologies, automated and streamlined workflows, and built a digital working environment to strengthen online collaboration within the organisation. Paperless meetings have become the main mode of holding meetings at the HKMA. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, various internal administrative matters are now handled mainly through electronic processes. In addition, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digital working modes, replacing paper-based documents and communications with digital means. At the same time, work on implementing an electronic records-keeping system is also underway. The above green and digital measures have brought about positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per capita, a significant reduction of 64.8% from 2015 (Figure 3). As most international events have returned to being held in physical form following the COVID-19 pandemic, and given the need to promote the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, it is inevitable that the relevant HKMA staff need to travel overseas on business. To reduce the carbon emissions caused by air travel, the HKMA encourages staff, where feasible, to take direct flights or to combine different business trips when participating in overseas events. At the organisational level, in 2023 the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO2e through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the HKMA also participated in a "Gold Standard"-certified carbon offset programme to offset the remaining carbon emissions caused by air travel; this programme carries out waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement processes take into account sustainability and environmental considerations. As part of a comprehensive review of the organisation's procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been formalised into an established system and complies with the environmental specifications of the Government's "Green Procurement List", particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. In addition, ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency have also been incorporated into the tender assessment criteria. At the same time, all suppliers must undertake to comply with environmental regulations. In accordance with the "4R" principles, namely Refuse, Reduce, Reuse and Recycle, the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimise waste generation and manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The breakdown of non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfill and various types of recyclable waste, is set out in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA directly participated for the first time in the red packet recycling programme run by the management company of the International Finance Centre office building. Staff handed in a total of about 3,000 used but still intact and like-new red packets. These red packets were subsequently handed over to an environmental organisation for distribution to the public for use in the following year's Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operational and back-up data centres account for a major part of the organisation's overall energy consumption, both data centres have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centres, achieving the best Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE). In 2023, the HKMA's two data centres were awarded "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" assessment guidelines issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organisation in Hong Kong to obtain these ratings. Improving the energy efficiency of the two data centres has all along been a key area of focus for the technical team. To this end, the team adopted green design in the fitting-out works and applied energy-efficient good practices to lower the PUE and achieve the relevant targets, including monitoring the environmental facilities of the data centres round the clock 24 hours a day and continuously improving environmental factors such as air flow and temperature settings. As the technical team continued to improve the energy use of the data centres, the HKMA engaged an external consultant in December 2021 to conduct a review, in order to comprehensively assess the green level of the data centres and formulate recommendations to further enhance performance in various aspects. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the completion of the study, the HKMA also began preparations to qualify for the "Green Data Centre" certification under the "BEAM Plus" certification scheme. The certification process is very comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the technical team rolled out optimisation measures based on the recommendations in the consultant's report, enhancing energy performance as well as the health elements of the working environment within the data centres.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2023 Data included total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, and non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste) for 2023, their respective intensities, and the changes in these data compared with the 2015 level. In addition, the 2023 Data also included the amount of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared with the level when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, and also covered the relevant data for the period from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (except for food waste). The scope of verification covered a total of 5 office and warehouse assets, of which 4 offices were located at 1) Two International Financial Centres, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, and 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, with the warehouse at 5) Roxy Industrial Centre, located in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data, and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanism. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the 5 assets. This verification work was carried out in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and reach a conclusion so as to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing the selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the basic procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. The relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA was responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team did not participate in the process of preparing the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provided reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concluded: the 2023 Data are substantially accurate and reliable; the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024

The threats posed by climate change are imminent, making it urgent to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record, and also the first year in which the global temperature exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased slightly during the COVID-19 pandemic, they have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current measures to mitigate climate change. In the process of addressing global warming, the emergence of climate-related risks is set to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Moreover, the current geopolitical tensions, the increasingly fragmented global economic landscape, the potential aggravation of energy security concerns, coupled with an uncertain economic outlook, all present greater challenges for countries in tackling climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained funding support. Across the globe, Asia in particular faces the most severe transition challenges. As the World Economic Forum has pointed out, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth, but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a pivotal role in whether the world can successfully achieve the goal of net-zero emissions. As a leading international financial centres in Asia, Hong Kong needs to strengthen its leading role and make full use of the power of finance to support and drive the transition within the region. To this end, the HKMA last year unveiled the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda", which sets out our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating the concept of sustainable development into the core of the financial system. On one hand, our work focuses on enhancing the ability of the financial industry to address climate change-related risks, and on the other hand, it emphasizes helping the industry seize the related new opportunities. At the same time, we lead by example and play a pioneering role. The HKMA's sustainable development work encompasses four major areas: supporting the banking sector towards net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and driving more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a key role in the net-zero transition of Hong Kong and Asia, but it also faces considerable risks during the transition process. In the "Action Agenda", we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive to achieve net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or before, and net-zero emissions in their financing by 2050 or before. At the same time, we require all banks to strengthen disclosures related to climate change risks and opportunities. While continuously enhancing banks' climate risk management, we also provide guidance for banks' transition planning to help them improve their capacity to cope with the transition and better manage the related risks. We are also carrying out preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with a view to further enhancing the industry's transparency in relevant activities. In addition, we are enhancing the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance launched in May last year, to incorporate more sustainable activities (including transition activities). We hope that by providing clear criteria, we can guide more capital towards sustainable and transition-related projects. Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks, which may affect the long-term financial performance and value of the Exchange Fund's investment projects. But at the same time, it also brings opportunities for growth and driving positive impact for the Exchange Fund. Our experience proves that investment returns and positive sustainable impact can be reconciled, and there is no conflict between them. In view of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "portfolio" by 2050 or before, and in the "Action Agenda" we pledged to support Asia's climate transition through the Exchange Fund's investments. At present, sustainable investment already accounts for more than 10% of the "portfolio". To further promote sustainable investment within the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation in November last year, to accelerate the transition to a low-carbon economy in Asia through co-investment. In addition, we released the first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document in September last year, to further encourage fund managers to proactively exercise asset ownership and adopt good sustainable investment practices. Capital mobilization is particularly important for accelerating the region's transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred location for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers (including mainland provincial and municipal governments), Hong Kong plays an important role in guiding capital to accelerate the region's transition. The "Action Agenda" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred sustainable financing platform, as well as the goal of promoting innovation in sustainable finance. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive innovation in green bonds (including the issuance in February last year of the world's first batch of multi-currency digital bonds), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" in May last year to cover transition financing instruments, and to the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme" launched in November last year, we have been committed to encouraging issuers in the region to use Hong Kong's financial platform to raise the funds needed for their decarbonization transition. To achieve a robust transition, in addition to capital and innovation, an inclusive and easily accessible sustainable development ecosystem is also needed for support.
