This includes reliable sustainability data, highly transparent information disclosure, and industry talent equipped with the relevant knowledge and skills. In this regard, in the "Action Agenda" we pledged to support the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosure, and to work towards filling the gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made good progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainability disclosure, in particular by providing convenient and easy-to-use climate disclosure templates to promote sustainability disclosure by small and medium-sized enterprises. In November last year, we also launched the "Green and Sustainable Finance" professional-level module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking, to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. In addition, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we enabled people from all walks of life to participate in discussions on sustainable development, thereby promoting cooperation and innovation. Within the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring that our operations align with the vision of sustainable development. In the "Action Agenda", we pledged to achieve net-zero emissions in our own operations by 2030 or before, which is 20 years ahead of our original commitment. In addition, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap promulgated by the Government. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024, and have incorporated low-carbon emissions as a screening factor in the procurement process. At the same time, we continue to improve work efficiency through digitalization, foster a culture of sustainable development within the organization, and motivate staff to actively participate in sustainable development work. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change, but the reshaping of the international landscape and drastic changes in the geopolitical situation have added uncertainties to global climate action. Nevertheless, climate change is an indisputable fact, and it is gradually intensifying. In the work of addressing climate change, the current situation does not allow us any slackening whatsoever. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help reduce the impact of climate risk on Hong Kong's financial system, and bring us opportunities in the process. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, striving to advance our sustainable development work and deepen relationships with like-minded partners. Despite the severe challenges we face, we will, as always, remain committed to supporting Hong Kong, Asia, and other regions in building a sustainable future.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the present generation. As one of the world's international financial centres and a sustainable finance hub within Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across Asia and the world. In October 2024, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), setting out the HKMA's vision in this area, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving various goals, and how we expect the industry to work together to advance the relevant efforts. Through formulating strategic policies, strengthening supervisory engagement, and enhancing internal operations, the HKMA plans to reinforce the capacity of Hong Kong's financial industry and the HKMA itself to address climate risk, and to promote Asia's transition towards a more sustainable economy. By actively participating in international and regional discussions, the HKMA is also committed to exerting its influence and taking part in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at the regional and global levels. As a banking sector regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness throughout the transition to net zero. Our top priorities in 2025 include: - launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices, and conducting a third round of consultation sessions, to review the implementation of the HKMA's relevant supervisory requirements by banks and to further strengthen banks' climate risk management capabilities; - refining the work of incorporating climate risk stress-tested scenarios into the HKMA's supervisor-driven stress-tested framework; - continuing to advance the work of incorporating climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review process; - commencing preparatory work on formulating relevant supervisory requirements for the local banking sector to implement the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks and the International Financial Reporting Standards on Sustainability Disclosure (ISSB Standards); - completing the compilation of the new module GS-2 of the "Supervisory Policy Manual" to provide banks with guidance on transition planning; and - sharing with the industry good practices on climate risk management and the application of green fintech. In addition to being a banking sector regulator, the HKMA also plays the role of a facilitator, committed to promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for the transition. We have released the first phase of the "Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance," providing the industry with tools to identify green and sustainable economic activities and to facilitate the related funding. The HKMA has commenced the second phase of the Taxonomy to expand its coverage, including adding transition elements, increasing green economic activities, and incorporating climate change adaptation objectives. In addition, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will hold another green fintech event in 2025 to promote banks' adoption of green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well positioned to support the sustainable financing needs of the region. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme," whose expanded coverage will include sustainable projects such as socially responsible projects. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bonds market and serve as a demonstration for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide subsidies through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable funds. We will also step up promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises from the Mainland and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing subsidies to prospective issuers of the digital green bond through the "Digital Bond Grant Scheme." Although market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures by institutions and enterprises is growing, different entities vary in their capabilities and readiness to make sustainability disclosures, and some entities may require additional guidance and support. In view of this, the HKMA will continue to work with other members of the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group to make sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. For example, we will continue to provide banks and their customers with richer climate disclosure tools, including easy-to-use sustainability disclosure templates and supporting tools; explore how to leverage technology to further make existing resources more convenient and user-friendly; and collaborate with major local industry organisations to provide the training the industry needs. The sustainable finance market is ever-changing, and there is a need to expand the local talent pool and fill knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key work in 2025 includes collaborating with the banking sector to develop professional-level training courses for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Enhanced Competency Framework for Banking Practitioners," and identifying areas where the industry has further training needs through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026 to 2030" study. In addition, we plan to work with key stakeholders to step up promotion of the government-funded "Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Training Programme" and to review the programme's scope of applicability. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to work with the International Finance Corporation through the "Alliance for Green Commercial Banks" to launch dedicated initiatives across Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing insightful market analysis, offering targeted skills upgrading and training support, fostering community connections, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to help banks develop roadmaps for making green finance a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net zero for the exchange Fund's investment portfolio by or before 2050, in support of the transition of the overall economy. Through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, we will continuously enhance the sustainability of the exchange Fund's investments, focusing mainly on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that promote positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to leading by example in institutional sustainability efforts. In line with the timeline for accelerating the achievement of the net zero commitment as announced in the "Action Agenda," the HKMA will progressively and pragmatically incorporate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting, continuing to advance the institution's sustainable development. Specifically, in 2025 we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring that we focus on material issues. In addition, we will conduct an energy audit and use technology solutions to assess the material impact of climate risk on our offices and operations, so as to enhance our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the "Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap" published by the Government and are actively carrying out preparatory work to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB Standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment by selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects in accordance with energy-efficiency and energy-saving principles. We will also expand digital measures to promote sustainable development and enhance efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and improving the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the general public.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to reducing its impact. Through its multiple roles as a central banking institution, a banking sector regulator, a market facilitator, a responsible investor and a sustainable development organisation, the HKMA contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the Asian region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework to lead the formulation of its relevant strategies and policies; oversee the implementation of relevant measures; and ensure that sustainability factors are integrated into the HKMA's own operations and working practices. In its commitment to sound institutional governance, the HKMA has put in place a robust sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and a high degree of transparency for its sustainability-related work. This governance framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively incorporated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and provides effective mechanisms to monitor and assess the progress and effectiveness of sustainability efforts. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: - the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which are responsible for monitoring the HKMA's work, including its sustainability efforts, and making recommendations; - the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which is responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; - in respect of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, which is responsible for coordinating and overseeing ESG-related work within the Exchange Fund Investment Office; and - in respect of other functional areas, the relevant teams and working groups responsible for planning and implementing relevant sustainability measures in banking and market development as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group), co-initiated by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion in the scope of the HKMA's various sustainability efforts over the years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability work across the HKMA's different functional areas. The Steering Committee is responsible for: - Providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking, green and sustainable finance ecosystem development, Exchange Fund investment and internal operations; - Overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; - Assessing the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - Overseeing the external communication strategy. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives as permanent members. In addition, we invite the dedicated Assistant Chief Executives of key functions related to green and sustainable development matters to attend the Steering Committee meetings to report on the major outcomes and future plans of their work. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's banking departments, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA and the SFC co-initiated the establishment of the Steering Group in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts on the financial industry's response to climate and environmental risks, so as to strengthen Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and among global financial centres. For details of the Steering Group's work, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Development of the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem".

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system in coping with climate risk, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impact of various sustainability and climate-related matters in their day-to-day business operations, and must therefore proactively manage climate risk. At the same time, banks play an important role in the financial system in channelling funds towards green and sustainable projects. As the regulator of the banking sector, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capabilities to address and manage climate risk, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economy. In October, the HKMA published the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), setting out the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as the region's sustainable finance centre and to support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The "Action Agenda" comprises eight major goals across four dimensions. To assist the industry in achieving the goals of the relevant banking policies, we have been undertaking the following work. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions in their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero emissions in their financing by 2050 or earlier. All banks are enhancing transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched an industry consultation on the draft of module GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capabilities in addressing the net-zero transition, as well as on related risk management. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of incorporating into the assessment process the relevant factors put forward by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) for the effective management of climate-related financial risks, and encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) to address climate risk. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analysing the latest developments in sustainability disclosure, and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a study on the technical feasibility of adopting the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the "Action Agenda". In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance (the Taxonomy) to address the industry's concerns about greenwashing and to help channel funds towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, and aims to be aligned with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of Mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating relevant elements in light of local circumstances. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope covered by the Taxonomy, and are consulting a wide range of stakeholders to further facilitate the intermediation of green and sustainable funds. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management, and was committed to supporting banks in building their capabilities to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to address climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under the two-year plan formulated in 2022 to incorporate climate risk into the banking supervisory process. To promote banks in strengthening their climate risk management capabilities, the HKMA shared with the banking sector good practices observed in thematic reviews and consultation meetings, mainly including: - Establishing a sound governance structure that clearly sets out the responsibilities of the board and senior management; - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters: (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) building a sound climate risk culture within the organisation. In August, the HKMA held a balanced supervisory roundtable on the theme of climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on a number of climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing, and helped inform the HKMA's work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA launched a round of thematic reviews of banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, and assessed their soundness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The thematic reviews covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress-tested. The HKMA held a second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual, and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest supervisory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance based on the specific circumstances of individual banks to support their climate risk management efforts. The HKMA completed the second round of banking sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) in 2024, with a total of 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups participating. The results showed that under various scenarios (including a hypothetical scenario in which climate risk and a macroeconomic downturn occur simultaneously), the Hong Kong banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot exercise, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risk. A report setting out the CRST results and the good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. The HKMA understands that banks encounter numerous data and methodology-related challenges in climate risk management, and has therefore been committed to a range of initiatives to promote the application of technology to address these challenges. To tackle the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for conducting climate risk assessments, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to assess the potential impact of physical risks on Hong Kong's residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform in light of user feedback and by incorporating more local data. In addition, the HKMA collaborated with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the financial services industry as a whole. During the year, we published an Application Practice Guide and two "Regtech Use Case Reports" (in English), setting out technology solutions used for environmental, social and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as for greenwashing risk management. We also held the third "FiNETech", bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore green fintech collaboration. The HKMA is well aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its ongoing monitoring work. The HKMA takes climate change into account in its continuous monitoring of financial stability risks, and has incorporated analysis of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Workstream under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, assisting central banks and regulators in understanding the macroeconomic and financial impact of climate change. In November, the NGFS published the fifth edition of its long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessment. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analysing the interaction between the transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to examine climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the "Practical Guide for Banks' Application of Green Technology" (in English), providing financial institutions with best practices for leveraging green technology to facilitate their net-zero transition. On the research front, the HKMA conducted a number of applied research projects to explore the impact of climate change on the financial industry and the economy as a whole. Research topics included the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in withstanding monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial industry in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The above research findings not only deepened our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability, but also provided valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, helping to inform the formulation of relevant policies. On the local front, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. The research findings were also shared with a broad range of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the HKMA Research Memorandum. The Hong Kong Institute for Monetary and Financial Research (the Research Centre), the research arm under the Academy of Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission firms can gain significant benefits from carbon pricing, and highlights its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission firms. The study was featured in the Research Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research" and shared with local and international academics and policy researchers. The HKMA's "Liquidity Facilities Framework" is a collateralised standby liquidity facilities arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into its assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risk and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, we help facilitate international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draw on the lessons learned to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in the region, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As set out in the HKMA's Sustainable Finance Action Agenda (the Action Agenda), the HKMA is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to developing Hong Kong into a preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green segment of the financial markets, enhancing the industry's sustainability disclosures, expanding the local green talent pool, and addressing the knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region.  Develop Hong Kong into a preferred sustainable financing platform in the region and globally Catalyse sustainable finance innovation Support high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosures Bridge the talent and knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in the region  To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and liveable city, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Programme in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds totalling approximately US$28 billion equivalent, sold to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds raised have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, and energy efficiency and conservation. We have seized every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, laying the groundwork for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the impact of the programme and further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope of the programme was expanded to cover sustainable projects and it was renamed the Government Sustainable Bond Programme (Sustainable Bond Programme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report, detailing the allocation of proceeds raised by green bonds and the expected environmental benefits.  In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing institutional green bonds of approximately US$3 billion equivalent under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This tri-currency issuance covered bonds of various tenors denominated in renminbi, US dollar, and euro. These bonds attracted a wide range of investors and received an enthusiastic subscription response, recording subscription amounts of over US$15 billion equivalent. Among them, the 20-year and 30-year renminbi green bonds were issued by the Government for the first time and were the longest-tenor renminbi bonds issued by the Government to date, providing a new benchmark for the market and further reinforcing the demonstration effect of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the choice of CNH investment products in Hong Kong. In addition, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the green bonds issued by the Government reflects investors' recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development.  To encourage more borrowers in the region to utilise Hong Kong's financing platform to raise funds for sustainable development, the HKMA continued to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme launched in May 2021, providing subsidies to eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The scheme has been well received by the industry, and as at the end of 2024, it had granted subsidies to approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totalling over US$140 billion. The scheme was extended by three years to 2027 in May 2024, and its scope of subsidies was expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the scheme is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries in the region to utilise Hong Kong's transition financing platform to progressively reduce carbon emissions. - Granted subsidies to approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, totalling over US$140 billion (as at the end of 2024) - Extended by three years to 2027, and expanded the scope of subsidies to cover transition financing instruments  Meanwhile, the HKMA actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, and the relevant work achieved satisfactory results. Among them, the Shenzhen Municipal People’s Government issued offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong for the fourth time in August, totalling RMB7 billion, comprising RMB2.7 billion of green bonds, RMB1 billion of sustainable bonds, and RMB900 million of social responsibility bonds. In September, the People’s Government of Guangdong Province issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the first time, totalling RMB5 billion, including RMB1.5 billion of green bonds. In October, the People’s Government of Hainan Province also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, totalling RMB3 billion, comprising RMB1 billion of blue bonds and RMB1 billion of sustainable bonds. The above bond issuance activities once again highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable fund flows between the Mainland and around the world.  With the above measures, Hong Kong has been able to consolidate its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub in Asia for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in 2024, with the total amount of such bonds arranged in Hong Kong reaching US$43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total.  To catalyse sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two batches of landmark tokenised green bonds in 2023 and 2024, being the world's first tokenised government green bond and the world's first multi-currency digital bond respectively. These issuances demonstrated the Government's support for market participants in applying asset tokenisation and innovative technologies in the field of green and sustainable finance in the region. The HKMA also launched the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including the digital green bond, thereby encouraging and supporting the innovative development of Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance market.  The working group on sustainability disclosures under the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Steering Group (the Steering Group) has been making efforts on Hong Kong's adoption of the International Financial Reporting Standards Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards). In December 2024, the Government published the Roadmap on Sustainability Disclosure in Hong Kong, providing a clear pathway for large publicly accountable entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been working closely with local and international partners to provide support to entities at different stages of preparedness in achieving high-quality sustainability disclosures, making sustainability disclosures more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continued to encourage the use of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies (the Questionnaire) launched by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template to facilitate sustainability disclosures by companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to facilitate online submission by companies (see the QR code below). The HKMA is refining the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, with specific measures including selecting the core questions in the Questionnaire and providing common usage scenarios for the Questionnaire. In addition, we are also striving to enhance the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information about the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage.  The HKMA leads by example by making high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report in accordance with the latest global standards, to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content on the HKMA's climate-related operational risks, as well as its plans and implementation progress in achieving climate goals. For details of the sustainability disclosures relating to our own operations, please refer to the chapter "Sustainable HKMA".  Given the rapidly changing sustainable finance market, and to bridge the knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is strengthening skills training in the banking sector, as well as promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners in sustainable finance, the HKMA, together with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the Foundation Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Enhanced Competency Framework for banking practitioners in July 2023. The module aims to help professionals in the banking sector acquire knowledge and develop relevant professional competencies in green and sustainable finance in a more effective manner, and covers four main work areas: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainability/climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosures and reporting; and (4) sustainability strategy, compliance, and controls. In addition, the Professional Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, targeting middle and senior banking practitioners responsible for relevant work, was also launched in November. To provide the necessary training to banking practitioners, the HKIB, as the administering body of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the Foundation Level training course of the module in May. Following the launch of the Professional Level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking sector in 2025 to develop the Professional Level training course.  To understand the further skills and training needs of the banking sector, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the banking sector to conduct the study "Future Banking Talent 2026 to 2030", with the aim of publishing the study results in 2025. This joint study is a follow-up to the "Future Banking Talent 2021 to 2025" paper published in June 2020. The results of the follow-up study will provide important reference for the industry, helping it to formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector.  Through its collaboration with the Steering Group, the HKMA also continued to assist in implementing the government-funded Pilot Green and Sustainable Finance Capacity Building Support Scheme, subsidising practitioners, graduates, and students to receive sustainable finance-related training. As at December 2024, a total of 85 international and local courses were registered as eligible training courses under the scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications had been approved. The Government announced in the 2025-26 Budget that the scheme would be extended to 2028.  The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international collaboration. As a founding member of the Capacity-building Alliance of Sustainable Investment (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-organised a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, with discussions centred on the global sustainable finance market, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. In addition, the HKMA supported the establishment of a chapter of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October, and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the HKMA actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can complement each other, the HKMA upholds the philosophy of responsible investment in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritising sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership. The HKMA invests prudently in accordance with the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value appreciation", believing that giving full attention to environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors helps reduce related investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a firm signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment work. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the pressing issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and striving for more favourable risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to advancing the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA released the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to investment partners through the annual ESG workshop and the HKMA website. We partner with like-minded investors, regulators and international organisations to jointly develop industry practices and standards, and to promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial industry and the central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future in which finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA announced the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"), which sets out the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's portfolio by 2050 and mobilising partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, further reinforcing its commitment to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The foremost guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practise responsible investment while balancing the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing the ESG and climate-related risks involved in the Exchange Fund's investments. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management approach, and monitors related implementation through regular meeting reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office, chaired by the Chief Strategist, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the various ESG initiatives of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. The motions and progress of work discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainability Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategist of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, meets regularly to provide guidance on the ESG policies and measures across the HKMA's various functions, including the Exchange Fund Investment Office, in order to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with the various teams of the Exchange Fund Investment Office on integrating ESG factors, and assists the senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office in managing the ESG, and particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various types of investments: - Public market investments – The Credit, Regulations and Monitoring Committee, comprising senior staff of the Exchange Fund Investment Office, reviews the integration of ESG factors into the credit risk model with reference to the input of the Sustainable Investment Team, and monitors the ESG status of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reporting by the Risk Management and Compliance Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Team also participates in the selection, appointment and monitoring of external investment managers of the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (for details, please refer to the section "Promoting Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" under the "Risk Management" section on page 39). - Private market investments – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the ESG-related assessments made by the Private Markets Investment and Risk Management teams on each investment proposal. The HKMA recognises that the physical and transition risks brought about by climate change, as well as the related opportunities, will affect the long-term financial performance of the Exchange Fund's investments. The "Emissions Gap Report 2024" published by the United Nations Environment Programme projects that, unless there is large-scale global mobilisation to rapidly cut greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties in policy changes, technological developments and behavioural shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuation. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also pose additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investments. Amid these challenges, as governments and industries shift towards sustainable solutions, they also create potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG factors. The HKMA has set the goal of achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's portfolio by 2050, and continues to advance its work through an orderly three-pronged approach to achieve this goal (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA announced the "Action Agenda", which consolidated the Exchange Fund's climate transition-related commitments and efforts (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA prefers proactive engagement over exclusion or divestment from investable assets. Investing in a sustainable future — achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's portfolio by 2050 - Actively expanding the scope and types of sustainable investments, especially climate transition-themed investments in public and private markets - Integrating ESG factors into all investment decisions, with particular attention to climate change and transition outlook considerations - Establishing clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, and requiring all external investment managers, investee companies and counterparties to comply with them - Committing to reduce the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from the 2017 level by 2030 Supporting regional transition through investment - Continuing to engage with external investment managers to optimise investment opportunities that drive transition - Continuing to identify and prioritise high-quality investment opportunities that facilitate Asia's transition and bring positive impact globally First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the Exchange Fund's foremost investment objective. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially affecting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA is able to seize opportunities to invest in companies that are undergoing transition and possess superior technology and good corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including companies in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transition of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding related investments or divesting does not help resolve the issue of carbon emissions. On the contrary, the HKMA supports these industries through the deployment of strategic capital and the active exercise of asset ownership, driving them to transition to sustainable and low-carbon practices, thereby bringing beneficial change for both themselves and the world. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from favouring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, in order to drive comprehensive decarbonisation across the economy as a whole. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio depends not only on the portfolio's own adjustments, but also on a broad economic transition. Although there is no perfect single solution, in 2024 the HKMA refined its responsible investment strategies, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the net-zero goals of the Exchange Fund and the world. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors and stewardship into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonisation tilting, and thematic investments in various assets aligned with net-zero emission pathways. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio towards ESG leaders or climate solution providers, complemented by stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, there may be greater focus on transition-enabling investments. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can facilitate climate transition while also enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund's portfolio, with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public market investments – The HKMA launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and extended the application of the customised low-carbon equity index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA also continues to seek green, social and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide funding for sustainable projects while offering competitive returns (for a related case study, see the section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds"). - Private market investments – The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA also actively identifies and reviews investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through establishing strategic partnerships with multinational organisations (for examples, see the section "Jointly Addressing Climate Challenges in Asia and Globally"). - Passive portfolios benchmarked against ESG indices - Customised decarbonisation strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios benchmarked against non-ESG indices - Governance-themed active portfolios - Active ESG portfolios themed on sustainability and climate transition - Projects with sustainable features, such as renewable energy infrastructure, as well as green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds themed on energy transition and decarbonisation across the globe, Asia and the Global South - Green, social and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organisation - The Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Programme (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation and focused on investing in sustainable projects in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" programme, which provides Paris Agreement-aligned climate-related investments in emerging markets The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a quasi-governmental institution. The proceeds raised by the green bonds were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading the ageing equipment of several sewage treatment facilities. These upgrade projects covered optimising monitoring and control systems and pump performance, in order to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction and recycling processes. In addition to continuously treating wastewater and sludge, these facilities compost or repurpose the dewatered sludge to produce fertiliser, charcoal, cement and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilise the gas generated during the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity. The HKMA invested in green bonds issued by a multilateral development bank. The bonds provide funding for multiple projects, including the rehabilitation of a country's canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess water flow from rivers to arid areas. The main purpose of the project is to rehabilitate the deteriorating canal lining, in order to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water-use efficiency and reclaim flooded areas. In addition, the project also carries out skills training for local stakeholders, promoting the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation techniques such as micro-irrigation, as well as sustainable farming practices.

The HKMA is committed to being a responsible and sustainable organisation. One of the HKMA's key priorities in 2024 in fulfilling this commitment was its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations to 2030—20 years ahead of the original target—in line with the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda". In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is also committed to fostering staff training and physical and mental well-being, and to advancing financial inclusion as well as enhancing the public's financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is the principal decision-making body for the organisation's various sustainability initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to addressing climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 the HKMA's new target of achieving net-zero emissions in its corporate operations by 2030, as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Agenda" (the "Action Agenda"). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Corporate Development and Operations) provides guidance on the implementation of sustainability measures relating to corporate operations, staff physical and mental well-being, and community engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Division serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, communicating, and reporting on the organisation's sustainability measures. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Team, comprising staff from various operational departments, provide an additional layer of support; the former is a platform for brainstorming and putting forward suggestions on how to create a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its staff, and society as a whole, The Hong Kong Council of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15 Years Plus Caring Organisation" logo for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: environmental, staff, and social responsibility. - Focusing on decarbonisation and digitalisation of the HKMA's daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 - Adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines - Promoting more environmentally friendly practices to the financial industry and the wider community - Building an engaged workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives - Creating a working environment that fosters collaboration and caring inclusion, values diversity, and strengthens staff sense of belonging - Providing a quality working environment that promotes healthy lifestyles - Cultivating a culture of caring for society - Incorporating social considerations into procurement procedures and supply chain management - Promoting financial inclusion and enhancing the public's financial literacy through consumer education activities. The HKMA is attentive to climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to bring forward the target date for achieving net-zero emissions in its own corporate operations to 2030—20 years ahead of its original commitment—as part of the "Action Agenda". The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards a net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of its daily operations, with an emphasis on reducing carbon emissions, saving energy, cutting paper use, and recycling waste, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix for power generation by local electricity companies. In addition, the HKMA is building a digitalised working environment to enhance efficiency while reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, the HKMA recognises the importance of cultivating a culture of sustainability, and therefore encourages staff to actively adopt practices conducive to sustainability through ongoing promotional programmes and activities. Under the overarching 2030 net-zero emissions target, the HKMA has been exploring the use of carbon insetting tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, and low-carbon procurement wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset the carbon emissions from air travel through purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset schemes. The HKMA will expand its carbon insetting and offsetting programmes to cover all remaining major carbon emissions. Beyond the aforementioned environmental commitments relating to its actual operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, from introducing electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for recirculation in the market. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as promoting staff physical and mental well-being and caring for society. Under the HKMA's overall enterprise-wide risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats faced in the HKMA's daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and reviewed their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, the design of the HKMA's offices incorporates a number of measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fire, and other emergencies. In addition, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only its offices but also its communications and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts evacuation and back-up facility drills on a regular basis to ensure that staff are always ready to carry out contingency measures. The HKMA has also been monitoring the transition risks it faces by tracking the greenhouse gas emissions generated by its own operations, waste generation, and energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's latest climate target is to achieve net-zero Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions related to its corporate operations by 2030. These targets were set with reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative. The HKMA measures and reports its organisational emissions using the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from petrol vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's main greenhouse gas emissions are Scope 2 indirect greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the consumption of fossil fuels for electricity generation. In the absence of supplier-specific data, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate its main Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfill and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are set out in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and basis of the Agency's verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" attached at the end of this report. The HKMA leads by example, upholding the same climate-related standards that it expects of the banks it regulates and the financial system it oversees. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its petrol vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024, and will continue this effort in 2025 to achieve fully green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in the various renovation works carried out in 2024, the HKMA reused existing furniture and fitting-out materials or traded in old items for discounts on new ones, thereby reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews the energy consumption and energy-saving measures of its offices and data centre, and in the 2024 data centre facility upgrade project adopted a modular-designed uninterruptible power supply system, further optimising the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centre. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency at partial loads, and features advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. Through its digital workplace, the HKMA has strengthened internal virtual collaboration and, coupled with streamlined workflows, has effectively reduced paper consumption. In addition, the HKMA extends the service life of its mobile and desktop devices in line with manufacturers' software update cycles, thereby prolonging the secure usage period of the devices. To reduce office waste, the HKMA follows the "4R" principles—refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. The HKMA has recycling bins for different materials at a number of convenient locations in its offices. To improve the recycling rate, the HKMA added recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit netting bags in 2024. In addition, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent the food waste it collects to a waste-to-energy centre in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA joined the Environmental Protection Department's "Waste Reduction Charter for Events", pledging to take measures to reduce the waste generated by its various events. The HKMA continues to give priority to procuring goods that meet the environmental specifications of the government's "Green Procurement List", particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan their trips carefully, such as combining multiple trips as far as possible when attending overseas events. At the organisational level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing its annual air travel carbon emissions by about 10%. In addition, the HKMA participates in a "Gold Standard"-certified carbon offset scheme to offset the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this scheme focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the HKMA arranged a range of learning activities for staff, such as talks and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance staff understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on 22 April 2024 through the whole of May, the HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month", themed "Think Green, Live Green, Work Green". This was a good opportunity for the HKMA to promote its commitment and drive towards environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The programme comprised a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" encouraging staff to practise green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and an indoor plant care workshop for "kokedama", a practice originating from Japan; it also shared the results of the waste audit, with a community recycling centre operator introducing best practices in recycling. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month", the HKMA launched a recycling campaign of around six months in October, highlighting the responsible handling of waste and reminding staff that pulling together their small changes in habits can greatly enhance the organisation's overall recycling performance. One highlight of the campaign was the launch of a "Green 'Fit' Action" video, in which several senior officers shared recycling tips. The campaign also introduced a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders to prompt staff to personally reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff questionnaire survey to understand their awareness of sustainability and to gather their views on the proposed green office measures. The survey results will help formulate future sustainability training activities and waste handling strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA regards itself as an important agent of change, and is therefore committed to leading efforts to accelerate the low-carbon transition and to encouraging the financial industry and society as a whole to adopt sustainable practices. The HKMA has introduced a number of measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the "Common Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's scope of services in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, in order to facilitate their submission of certain supervisory data. The purpose of expanding the platform's scope of services is to further simplify the submission process for reporting institutions and provide a smoother experience for all users, while reinforcing the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures launched in 2024 include the SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA questionnaire surveys through a simplified submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system, providing users with a central platform featuring advanced search functions for bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted an independent verification of the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (the "HKMA"). The Data include the total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and greenhouse gas emissions from air travel for 2024, as well as their respective intensities. In addition, the Data include Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions generated from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's greenhouse gas emissions data were prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol ("GHG Protocol") jointly published by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covered a total of six office and warehouse assets, among which five offices are located at 1) Two International Finance financial centres Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) One Pacific Place, 4) Kowloon Commerce Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and the warehouse is located at 6) Lai Sing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification was to provide reasonable assurance on the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the six assets. This verification work was performed in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised) "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed specifically to form an opinion and conclusion in order to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and also reviewed the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks, and conducted reliability tests. The verification process also included verifying the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with the representatives responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for examination. Relevant raw data and supporting evidence were also reviewed in detail during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the information. Our verification work was entirely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team was not involved in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provided reasonable assurance on the Data and concluded: - The Data are substantially accurate and reliable; - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanisms are adequate. Shum Siu-yan, Audit Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025
